Published online:
July 31, 2026 (Reuters)

Geographic focus:
United States

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical observation [YES] — PCE data, prior Fed decisions, bond yield movements referenced
T2. Forward-looking immediate [YES] — September FOMC decision, Jackson Hole (late August), summer inflation trajectory
T3. Long-term development [YES] — Potential inflation framework overhaul post-January, Fed strategy review by end of 2026

Synopsis:
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh held rates steady at 3.50%-3.75% while delivering hawkish inflation rhetoric without committing to rate hikes, triggering a bond selloff that pushed 30-year Treasury yields to a 19-year high above 5.2%. Three FOMC voting members dissented in favor of an immediate +25bps hike (Logan, Kashkari, Hammack). Core PCE remains elevated at 3.3% (June), well above the 2% target. Warsh also hinted at a potential inflation framework revision post-January 2027, adding further uncertainty. Markets are pricing skepticism — short-end yields fell while long-end yields surged (bear steepener). September is shaping up as a critical decision point, with internal Fed pressure building for a hike if inflation doesn't materially ease. Political constraint from the White House adds complexity to Warsh's path.
